# runpod_endpoint_worker_logs (Data Source)

Log lines from one Serverless worker. The API streams these live, so the read collects the backfill (tail lines, 100 by default) and returns as soon as it has them, or as soon as the stream goes quiet for idle_timeout_seconds, and in any case at read_timeout_seconds. Logs change between runs, so every plan shows this data source as needing a refresh.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The API streams worker logs live. The read collects the backfill (50 lines
# here) and returns; read_timeout_seconds caps how long it waits for them.
data "runpod_endpoint_worker_logs" "vllm" {
  endpoint_id          = "ep_abc123"
  worker_id            = "worker_abc"
  tail                 = 50
  read_timeout_seconds = 10
}

output "worker_log_text" {
  description = "The worker's recent output as one string."
  value       = join("\n", data.runpod_endpoint_worker_logs.vllm.lines)
}

output "resume_cursor" {
  description = "Cursor of the last event read; pass it back as last_event_id to continue from here."
  value       = data.runpod_endpoint_worker_logs.vllm.last_id
}
```

Complete, runnable configurations that use this data source live in the
use-case modules under `v2/modules/` in the provider repository; the Guides
section documents each one.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `endpoint_id` (String) Serverless endpoint identifier the worker belongs to.
- `worker_id` (String) Worker identifier, from runpod_endpoint_workers.

### Optional

- `idle_timeout_seconds` (Number) How long a gap in the stream ends the read, once at least one event has arrived. Defaults to 2. This is what returns a short backfill promptly instead of waiting out read_timeout_seconds, and it is not an error or a warning: a quiet stream means the history is exhausted.
- `last_event_id` (String) SSE reconnect cursor: a timestamp this endpoint emitted earlier, in RFC 3339 format, as reported by last_id. Takes precedence over since and tail, and the read is bounded only by read_timeout_seconds.
- `read_timeout_seconds` (Number) Hard bound on the read, for a stream that keeps producing output faster than idle_timeout_seconds. Defaults to 10, 1 to 60. Reaching it is not an error; the events collected so far land in state behind a warning. The ceiling is the provider's HTTP client, which closes the connection at 60 seconds.
- `since` (String) RFC 3339 timestamp to resume from. When set, tail is ignored and the read is bounded only by read_timeout_seconds.
- `source` (String) Log source to read: "container" for the container's stdout and stderr, or "system" for the host lifecycle stream. Omit for both.
- `tail` (Number) Number of historical lines to backfill, 0 to 5000. The API defaults to 100. The read returns as soon as that many events have arrived, or once the stream goes quiet for idle_timeout_seconds if the pod has less history than that. Set 0 to skip the backfill and collect only live lines. Ignored by the API when since or last_event_id is set.

### Read-Only

- `entries` (Attributes List) Log events in the order the API streamed them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries))
- `last_id` (String) Cursor of the last event received; pass it back as last_event_id to resume where this read stopped. Null when the read collected no event that carried one.
- `lines` (List of String) The line text of every entry, in the same order, for use with join() or file().

<a id="nestedatt--entries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entries`

Read-Only:

- `line` (String) The log line itself. An event whose payload is not the documented JSON object is reported here as its raw text.
- `source` (String) Log source that produced the line: container or system. Null for an event the API sent without one.
- `timestamp` (String) Event timestamp in RFC 3339 format; null for an event the API sent without one.
